prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. One standalone text-free Georgian-Persian manuscript miniature.
Medieval Georgian-Persian illuminated manuscript miniature painting for Shota Rustaveli's "The Knight in the Panther's Skin" (ვეფხისტყაოსანი). 16th–17th-century Georgian royal manuscript miniature, Mamuka Tavakarashvili / King Vakhtang VI illumination tradition blended with classical Persian-Safavid tempera miniature. Egg tempera, lapis lazuli, malachite green, vermilion, warm ochre and burnished antique gold leaf on aged ivory-parchment vellum. Stylized faceted rocky cliffs, ornamental cypress and pomegranate trees, intricately patterned arches and domes, expressive courtly figures in medieval Georgian-Eastern attire. Fine controlled contours, delicately patterned fabrics, luminous matte mineral pigments, slightly flattened layered miniature space with expressive narrative gestures. A painted manuscript scene, not photorealism, cinematic rendering, modern digital fantasy or a collage of circular portraits. Reuse referenced character faces and coloring but adapt costume to the actual chronological story scene; Tariel wears ordinary Indian court or military attire in early backstory, his panther skin belongs to his later exile. Exact horizontal 16:10 composition, preferably native 1600x1000 pixels, a single coherent scene framed for a card vignette. Soft natural painted vignette dissolving to warm aged ivory vellum at edges, modest antique-gold floral flourishes at the perimeter, no rigid border. Key faces and gestures comfortably inside the central safe area, no important content cut off. STRICTLY NO TEXT, NO LETTERS, NO CAPTIONS, NO NUMBERS, NO INSCRIPTIONS, NO CALLIGRAPHY, NO BANNERS, NO SCROLLS, NO SIGNATURES, NO WATERMARKS anywhere. Architectural ornament must be purely floral/geometric with no pseudo-writing. If letters are narratively necessary, use a small closed plain unmarked folded paper or sealed envelope, never visible writing or rolled scrolls. All book covers/pages must be plain and unmarked. Do not show graphic blood or gore; imply violent events through gestures, context and intact clothing.
Episode 23 — Return via the Cave to Arabia & Wedding of Avtandil and Tinatin.
Setting: Arabia, Rostevan and Tinatin's magnificent landward royal wedding court: a high gold-and-malachite palace arch, ivory columns, vermilion patterned carpets, flowering pomegranates, a distant dry blue mountain garden. NO coastal sea view here. Compose a NEW wider ceremonial tableau rather than copying the wedding composition in image5.
Scene: Avtandil and crowned Tinatin are the CENTRAL DOMINANT WEDDING COUPLE seated together on a purple-and-gold royal dais, gently joining hands and exchanging relieved affectionate looks. Elderly crowned Rostevan stands just behind them offering an open-handed blessing. Their four intimate guests flank the dais: Tariel and Nestan together to the left; Pridon and Asmat to the right. Exactly seven people, all in one coherent court. Small low bowls of fruit and jewels in the foreground; no officials, priests, documents, flags, hanging banners or scrolls. Keep each face and pair clearly separate and anatomically natural.
References: image1 is the established manuscript STYLE only (do NOT include the poet). Image2 is Avtandil's youthful clean-shaven olive face and wavy dark hair; dress him in silver-blue and crimson wedding attire with no helmet. Image3 is Tinatin's exact face, flowing black hair, purple-and-gold embroidered royal dress, large gold crown with central red jewel. Image4 is Rostevan's exact elderly face, long white hair and full white beard, broad jeweled gold crown and burgundy-gold robe. Image5 supplies the identities/costume colors of the FOUR SECONDARY GUESTS ONLY: Tariel curly dark hair and short beard in gold-and-coral attire; Nestan dark eyes and black veil, emerald-and-gold gown and emerald diadem; Pridon short dark hair and close beard/mustache with navy and rust cloak; Asmat simple charcoal hood with narrow gold trim. Do NOT make Tariel and Nestan the bridal couple in this new scene. Avtandil and Tinatin must be unmistakably central.
Exact horizontal16:10, same soft natural ivory vellum vignette. STRICTLY no text, letters, numbers, calligraphy, captions, inscriptions, banners, scrolls, seals with lettering or watermarks.

visual_qa.notes: Seven figures retained. Avtandil and Tinatin remain the central bridal couple; Pridon now stands separately behind the right dais with his own hands at his belt, while Asmat sits upright with hands in her own lap. No romantic head leaning or touching; both attend the central wedding. Other five figures, ornate style, text-free composition and native approximately16:10 aspect preserved.
